data.narrative:
Strata Robotics is a seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Eric Zhou and Alex Mason. The company has raised $5.2M to date. The relevant peer universe consists of 9 private robotics companies and 1 public comparable (ticker 277810.KQ), though the private peer set lacks sufficient depth at identical stage and valuation tier for reliable median-based triangulation.

The stage-progression method is the primary applicable approach, given data constraints. Using total raised of $5.2M as a proxy for current valuation and applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage advancement yields an implied valuation of $13M. Peer-median analysis was not feasible: while the broader robotics sector contains 10 comparable companies, filtering for same-stage or adjacent-stage peers with similar valuation tiers produced insufficient datapoints (fewer than 3) to support a robust median calculation, making sector-wide aggregation unreliable.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $11M (low) to $15M (high), with a midpoint of $13M. This range reflects the single applicable method and inherent stage-specific uncertainty. Key limitations include the thin seed-stage peer set in robotics, reliance on a single methodology, and lack of recent revenue or growth metrics to validate stage-progression assumptions. Material upside or downside would depend on commercial traction, capital efficiency, and competitive positioning relative to Walden Robotics, Divergent, and other named peers.
